description: Witness cases for tasks/tau-error-class-audit-2026-08.md (τ architecture review A1 + C1). A1: Spark-emulated analyzer errors exited as gRPC UNIMPLEMENTED with their Spark class buried in prose, so the oracle's ^\s*\[([A-Z][A-Z0-9_.]*)\] regex could only ever recover error_class=None — these cases were structurally unable to pass an error-class comparison, not merely red. C1: analyze_to_df omitted the source_quals clear its WithColumnsRenamed sibling performs, so τ resolved a qualified reference Spark rejects. Bonus: the audit also found τ rejecting five shapes Spark accepts.
reference_side_validated: 2026-08-06 — every expected_error below was OBSERVED via getCondition() against live Spark, and every no-error case was confirmed to return rows. No token in this manifest was inferred from source reading alone.

witnesses.pins: df.select(..).alias('t').toDF('a','b').select('t.a') — the pre-rename qualifier is dead. Spark: UNRESOLVED_COLUMN.WITH_SUGGESTION; τ used to RESOLVE it (leniency divergence).
witnesses.born_red_as: error-parity divergence — Spark raised, τ returned rows

witnesses.pins: union() arity mismatch now carries NUM_COLUMNS_MISMATCH instead of exiting UNIMPLEMENTED with no recoverable class.
toDF() arity mismatch carries ASSIGNMENT_ARITY_MISMATCH (not a toDF-specific class, which is why it had to be observed).
dropFields('nope') on a struct lacking it is a NO-OP in Spark — struct returned unchanged. τ used to reject, citing UpdateFields.scala::checkInputDataTypes; that reading was wrong.
witnesses.born_red_as: error-parity divergence — τ raised, Spark returned rows

witnesses.finding: A1-adjacent (third gap, found while building errcls-004)
witnesses.pins: UNALIASED dropFields projection. Data matches; only the auto-generated column name diverges — Spark names it 'update_fields(s, dropfield())', τ names it 'expr' because pretty_name has no UpdateFields arm. Same family as prettyname-004 (Window arm). errcls-004 carries an explicit alias so the over-strictness fix is tested independently of this.
witnesses.born_red_as: schema mismatch — Column 0 name: Reference='update_fields(s, dropfield())', Test='expr'
witnesses.not_a_regression: not in select_block_corpus_baseline.txt; documents a pre-existing pretty_name gap that this change surfaced rather than caused

witnesses.pins: unpivot variable name colliding with an id column is accepted by Spark, producing a DUPLICATE-named schema (id:bigint, id:string, v:double). Spark rejects ambiguous references, never duplicate names in a schema — τ's guard comment claimed the opposite.
witnesses.born_red_as: error-parity divergence — τ raised, Spark returned rows

witnesses.pins: recursive CTE with UNION (not ALL) → UNION_NOT_SUPPORTED_IN_RECURSIVE_CTE. The only one of the three prose pseudo-classes whose token was correct; it was still unrecoverable because it sat in the message rather than a leading [TOKEN].
LATERAL + NATURAL join → INCOMPATIBLE_JOIN_TYPES. The prose token said UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE, which is WRONG — no UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE subclass for natural joins exists among the 1244 conditions.
LATERAL + USING → the UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.LATERAL_JOIN_USING SUBCLASS. The prose token carried only the bare base class, so even the 'right' one was incomplete.

Four of the five surveyed cases where BOTH engines reject and Spark's class is PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR. GREEN since classify_parse_failure (parser_v2/mod.rs) upgrades the provably-malformed subset: 002 unbalanced delimiters, 003 expression required but input ended, 004 lexical failure, 005 expression required but slot empty. The three signals hold regardless of sqlparser's grammar coverage, which is why they cannot slander valid Spark.
witnesses.born_red_as: error-class divergence — expected [PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR], τ raised [None]; now green

witnesses.pins: SELECT * FROM emp VERSION AS OF 1 — τ fails at PARSE (sql::parse_error) but Spark parses it fine and fails in ANALYSIS with UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.TIME_TRAVEL. Proves a blanket sql::parse_error -> PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR mapping would emit the WRONG class, swapping one miscategorisation for another. Must fail loudly if anyone maps the category wholesale. Remains RED by design: under the classifier it correctly stays UNIMPLEMENTED, which is τ's honest answer since τ does not implement time travel at all. Making it green would require emitting UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE.TIME_TRAVEL, which is only Spark's answer for a temp view — on a Delta table Spark supports time travel and returns rows.
witnesses.not_a_regression: not in the baseline; guardrail for an open finding

witnesses.pins: `SELECT * FRM emp` IS malformed, but sqlparser reports `Expected: end of statement, found: FRM`, byte-identical in form to the shape produced by genuine τ grammar gaps (TRANSFORM -> `found: 'cat'`, VERSION AS OF -> `found: AS`, CREATE TABLE ... USING -> `found: USING`) — all of which Spark ACCEPTS. The shape carries no information, so no classifier can separate them without a Spark-grammar oracle.
witnesses.not_a_regression: not in the baseline; kept red deliberately. Will go green for free if sqlparser grows the missing constructs, shrinking the ambiguous set.

parse_layer_survey: 36 cases run against both τ and live Spark 4.1.1 (2026-08-07). Key counter-examples where sqlparser rejects but Spark ACCEPTS: HiveQL TRANSFORM, and CREATE TABLE ... USING parquet — recorded in tasks/tau-error-class-audit-2026-08.md rather than as corpus cases (TRANSFORM spawns a process; CREATE TABLE mutates catalog state). Survey also found Spark is permissive where one would not expect: 'SELECT * FROM emp WHERE' is ACCEPTED (WHERE parsed as a table alias), and 'SELECT id, FROM emp' raises TRAILING_COMMA_IN_SELECT rather than PARSE_SYNTAX_ERROR.
